[^comment-NYMXV05P2808A-1]: The identity of Muḥammad b. Isḥāq b. Kathīr b. Yasār is unknown and he is only listed in conjunction with this passage in the pre-modern corpus. <a href="../references.html#ref-TDSH" class="source-ref">TDSHV69P189B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAsākir</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh madīnat Dimashq</span>, vol. 69 p. 189) lists a Muḥammad b. Isḥāq b. Kathīr al-Ṣawrī, who apparently gave dictation to Abū al-Ḥasan Khaythumah b. Sulaymān and heard from Mūʾmmal b. Ismāʿīl. The editor of the text states that his name may have been Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm b. Kathīr. <a href="../references.html#ref-BNTH" class="source-ref">BNTHV09P144F</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn Ḥibbān</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Thiqāt</span>, vol. 9 p. 144) gives this name but does not list a date of death. <a href="../references.html#ref-TDSH" class="source-ref">TDSHV46P301B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>Ibn ʿAsākir</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh madīnat Dimashq</span>, vol. 46 p. 301), however, gives his name as Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm b. Kathīr b. Wafdān al-Ṣawrī, which would seem to eliminate him as the possible source. Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī gives two variations of the name: Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm b. Kathīr, Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ṣayfūrī who lived at the Syria Gate in Baghdād around 273/886 (see <a href="../references.html#ref-KHTG" class="source-ref">KHTGV02P283A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh Baghdād</span>, vol. 2 p. 283)) and a Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm b. Kathīr al-Ṣawrī but gives not biographical details (see <a href="../references.html#ref-KHTG" class="source-ref">KHTGV08P665A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh Baghdād</span>, vol. 8 p. 665)). According to <a href="../references.html#ref-KHTG" class="source-ref">KHTGV07P623A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh Baghdād</span>, vol. 7 p. 623), Jaʿfar b. ʿAbd al-Wāḥid’s kunyā was al-Hāshimī and Muḥammad b. Muḥammad b. Sulaymān is listed as al-Bāghandī. <a href="../references.html#ref-JJKX" class="source-ref">JJKXV02P396D</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Jurjānī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Kāmil fī ḍuʿafāʾ al-rijāl</span>, vol. 2 p. 396) states that Jaʿfar b. ʿAbd al-Wāḥid related from Wahb b. Jarīr, the son of the witness Jarīr b. Ḥāzim. He was also appointed Qāḍī of al-Baṣrah (<a href="../references.html#ref-KHRX" class="source-ref">KHRXV01P328B</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Khalīlī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>al-Irshād fī maʿrifah ʿulamāʾ al-ḥadīth</span>, vol. 1 p. 328)). He was also appointed chief judge of Rāʾy in 240/854 and died in 258/871 (<a href="../references.html#ref-KHTG" class="source-ref">KHTGV08P55A</a> (<span class='ref-author'>al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī</span>, <span class='ref-title'>Taʾrīkh Baghdād</span>, vol. 8 p. 55)).
